title.narrative: Provision of lifesaving nutrition assistance to the vulnerable communities affected by the climatic shocks in Beledweyne District, Hiran Region

description.narrative: ltpgtThe project aims to provide life-saving basic nutrition services, both curative and preventive, to vulnerable communities affected by climatic shocks in the Beledweyne district. The planned project will involve extensive community mobilization and sensitization through community health workers and meetings, aiming to raise awareness about the new program and the services available. Following this, WARDI will train and orient nutrition staff, including community health workers, on the integrated management of acute malnutrition. Additionally, community health workers will receive harmonized community-based training to Promote Maternal, Infant, Young Child, and Adolescent Nutrition (MIYCAN) through nutrition education, which will integrate essential messages about Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH), health, and food security.ltbrgtOnce the staff are fully trained, the nutrition team and the community health workers will conduct routine Mid-Upper Arm Circumference (MUAC) screenings to identify children with acute malnutrition. The target is to screen 24,000 children (12,240 girls and 11,760 boys) and 4,800 Pregnant and Lactating Women (PLW). Children diagnosed with severe acute malnutrition (SAM) without medical complications who pass the appetite test will be admitted to the Outpatient Therapeutic Program (OTP). Those with underlying medical conditions or who fail the appetite test will be referred for stabilization at Beledweyne General Hospital, which has been managed by WARDI since 2017ltbrgtWARDI plans to admit 2,200 children (1,122 girls and 1,078 boys) screened for acute malnutrition, along with 4,800 PLW, and to refer 840 children who have SAM with medical complications to Stabilization center (SC) managed by WARDI for further specialized treatment. Moderate acute malnutrition cases will also be identified through routine screenings and referred to the Targeted Supplementary Feeding Program (TSFP) at the same nutrition sites managed by WARDI and are supported by WFP grants. The proposed sites will also provide primary healthcare services through the Damal Cafimaad project, further strengthening the integration of services. ltbrgtTo anchor prevention activities at both facility and community levels, infant and young child feeding (IYCF) sessions will be initiated, combined mass Muac screening exercise to empower families to prevent and early identify acute malnutrition for prompt intervention. Approximately 3,200 people will have access to IYCF services through routine counseling sessions organized by trained IYCF counselors at the target nutrition sites. Using its technical support for national cold chain management in the Hiran region, WARDI will ensure that all sites deliver routine immunizations while identifying and referring children with serious illnesses. A team of community health workers will be recruited to handle community mobilization, MUAC screenings, tracking defaults for both nutrition and immunization programs, and referring cases of GBV. ltbrgtWARDI will collaborate closely with other stakeholders, including the Ministry of Health (MOH), Hirshabelle Regional Health Authority, and various clusters to ensure proper implementation of the project and that target communities are effectively reached. Furthermore, WARDI will create synergies between its planned nutrition and WASH projects, as well as other initiatives implemented in the target locations. Additionally, nutrition staff will receive IMAM and IYCF training integrated with on Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA), GBV and child protection to educate the community on how to report and identify such incidents, as well as on preventing Aid Diversion and Gender-Based Violence (GBV).
